chunks: They said: 'O Noah, you have argued with us, and disputed at length; so bring that (retribution) you promise, if you speak the truth.'
ai.seo_question: What did Noah's people demand of him to prove his truthfulness?
ai.summary: In this verse, the disbelievers of Noah (peace be upon him) mockingly demand the immediate execution of the promised punishment, revealing their arrogance and impatience for divine retribution. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a psychological tactic of the stubborn to test the prophet's sincerity, viewing their challenge as a precursor to the finality of the flood. This interaction underscores the theme of 'istikbar' (arrogance) as a barrier to accepting truth, a recurring motif in the narratives of the prophets.
